record.notes: The 'Server ab 2,45 EUR' banner is the entry rung of four ladders and none of them is 8 GiB. The EUR 2.45 plan is 1 vCPU / 2 GiB / 20 GB / 5 TB in Frankfurt. The 8 GiB shapes are EUR 3.95 on the 2026-Sale ladder and EUR 5.99 on the Xeon ladder, both marked 'Ausverkauft'. Twenty-one of twenty-four rungs across the four KVM pages are sold out; three Ryzen GEN 2 rungs say 'Jetzt konfigurieren'. The buyable 4 GiB row is the one priced here, at EUR 3.95 = USD 4.42 with 10 TB of traffic, which is the largest transfer allowance of any sub-USD-5 row found. EUR converted at 1.1193 (ECB reference 2026-10-23). No card hold is stated anywhere. Two things remain open: the rails actually offered at balance top-up (login wall at /cp/credit/add), and whether a debit or prepaid card is accepted (only 'Kreditkarte' is named). The public order pages rendered a signed-in session string and their price summary did not reconcile with the product-page price, so the absolute figure on those pages was not used; only their structural text was, and it agreed across two pages.

extras.price_arithmetic: EUR 3.95 a month, VAT inclusive, billed monthly, prepaid; 3.95 x 1.1193 USD/EUR (ECB reference rate for 2026-10-23, read 2026-10-24) = USD 4.42 a month. A VPS bills whether it runs or not, so the 24/7 and 10 h/day figures are the same number.
extras.renewal_note: no term discount and no first-term promo: every card reads 'Monatlich' with no strike-through price, and the order summary prints a 'Verlängerungsbetrag (30 Tage)' equal to the amount due today, so the renewal is the same monthly figure. The order page also describes the price as 'dauerhaft' (permanent).
extras.promo: the 2026-Sale page is named as a sale but states no end date and no post-sale price; the Ryzen ladder is not labelled a sale at all. The sale is capacity-limited, not time-limited: stock is released again when a server lapses, per the vendor's stock page.

record.notes: UNRECONCILED, and that is the finding. The sale page prices Starter at EUR 3.95 a month with 10 TB and DDR4. The order page for the same SKU is titled 'fur dauerhaft 3.95EUR' (permanently 3.95) but its own order summary computes 'Verlangerungsbetrag (30 Tage) 5,99 EUR' and 'Heute fallig 5,99 EUR', lists '1 TB Traffic' rather than 10 TB, and on the neighbouring Small SKU prints 'DDR3' where the sale page prints 'DDR4'. The script's basePrice is 3.95, so the 5.99 is not a base price plus an add-on the buyer chose. This is the DediRock pattern with an extra twist: the page and the cart disagree while both claim the same price. EUR 3.95 = USD 4.42 and EUR 5.99 = USD 6.71 at the ECB rate, so which one is real decides whether this row is under the line. The only honest statement is that the cart charges EUR 5.99 today and the page advertises EUR 3.95, and a buyer meets the cart. VERDICT: 'paid-only' because the figure the cart charges, EUR 5.99 = USD 6.71, is over the line; if the page's EUR 3.95 = USD 4.42 is the real price the row would qualify, and reconciling the two is the open question.
